text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.5% today, climbing to $412.85 after a sharp four-day rally that gained $23 from Monday's low. The move reflects a reversal in oil market sentiment: crude prices have stabilized and ticked higher over the past two days (US oil at $89.62, up from the dip below $90 earlier this week) as initial hopes for a near-term Iran peace deal have faded. Secretary of State Rubio signaled yesterday that negotiations remain stalled, countering Trump's earlier optimism, which likely reassured investors that geopolitical tension and oil demand won't collapse as quickly as feared.

Refinery utilization remains elevated at 95.2%, supporting margins for a refiner like Marathon even as crude prices stay moderate. The four-day bounce also follows heavy selling last week (the stock dropped 4.5% over two weeks through early November), so some of today's gain may reflect technical stabilization and profit-taking by sellers after the worst of the panic over Iran de-escalation passed.
